title: The Vision of Peace: March to Hudaybiyyah
subtitle: The Prophetic Dream, Garments of Ihram, and Fourteen Hundred Pilgrims
summary: The divine dream of peaceful pilgrimage, fourteen hundred companions donning white Ihram with seventy sacrificial camels, Quraysh's armed cavalry intercept, the rugged detour over Thaniyyat al-Murar, the halting of Al-Qaswa', and the miraculous spring of Hudaybiyyah.

sections.text: In the sacred month of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the sixth year of the Hijrah (628 CE), the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saw a true and luminous dream (Ru'ya Sadiqah). In the vision, he entered the sacred precinct of the Ka'bah in Makkah alongside his companions in absolute peace and tranquility, shaving their heads and trimming their hair, holding the key to the sanctuary without fear. Because the dreams of prophets are divine revelation, the Prophet ﷺ informed his companions, sparking boundless joy throughout Madinah after six agonizing years of exile from their beloved sanctuary.

The Prophet mobilized fourteen hundred—some narrations say fifteen hundred—companions. To demonstrate unequivocally to all of Arabia that this was a purely peaceful spiritual pilgrimage rather than a military assault, the Prophet commanded that none carry armor or weapons of war, permitting only sheathed traveler's swords. At the station of Dhu al-Hulayfah six miles south of Madinah, the pilgrims entered the sacred state of Ihram, donning two simple white unstitched cloths and driving seventy garlanded sacrificial camels (Hady) in their midst. Their voices rose in the desert, chanting the eternal hymn of submission: 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk!'

When news reached Makkah that fourteen hundred Muslims were approaching, the leadership of Quraysh was seized by furious paranoia and wounded pride. They feared that if Muhammad entered Makkah peaceably in broad daylight, all Arabia would mock Quraysh as being too weak to defend its ancient sanctuary. In violation of centuries of sacred Arabian tradition honoring peaceful pilgrims during the holy months, Quraysh mobilized their fighting men and dispatched an elite cavalry vanguard of two hundred horsemen under Khalid ibn al-Walid and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl to intercept and ambush the pilgrims at Kara' al-Ghamim.
The Detour & The Halting of Al-Qaswa'

Informed of Khalid's cavalry ambush by scouts from the Banu Khuza'ah, the Prophet ﷺ inquired: 'Who among you can lead us by a path other than the one where they await us?' A guide from Aslam led the pilgrims along a rugged, razor-sharp mountain pass known as Thaniyyat al-Murar, bypassing the hostile ambush entirely and bringing them out onto the edge of the sacred boundary at Hudaybiyyah, approximately nine miles west of Makkah.

As the vanguard reached the boundary, the Prophet's she-camel, Al-Qaswa', abruptly knelt down and refused to advance. The companions urged her to rise, shouting: 'She has become stubborn! Al-Qaswa' has refused!' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ corrected them gently: 'She has not become stubborn, nor is that in her nature; rather, He who restrained the Elephant (from entering Makkah) has restrained her!'

The Prophet then made a monumental proclamation of peace: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, Quraysh will not ask of me any term today wherein they venerate the sacred precincts of Allah, except that I shall grant it to them!' He then ordered the pilgrims to encamp around the dried-up, waterless watering hole of Hudaybiyyah.
The Miraculous Spring in the Desert

The companions complained of agonizing thirst as the sun beat down upon the arid stones and the well lay completely dry. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew an arrow from his quiver and handed it to Bara' ibn Azib or Najiyah ibn Jundub, commanding him to plant it firmly into the mud at the bottom of the well. The Prophet then supplicated to his Lord. In an instant, water gushed forth with miraculous abundance, rising to the rim of the well until fourteen hundred pilgrims and all their mounts drank to their fill and filled every waterskin.
Camped at the very gateway of Makkah with divine peace descending upon their hearts, the believers awaited the arrival of Makkan emissaries, poised on the knife-edge of war and peace.

references.title: The Holy Quran
references.author: Surah Al-Fath (48:27)
references.notes: Divine confirmation of the true vision granted to the Prophet ﷺ of entering the Sacred Mosque in safety.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.source: Kitab al-Shurut, Bab al-Shurut fi al-Jihad wa al-Musalahah, Hadith 2731–2732
references.notes: Bukhari 2731–2732 is the long narration of Hudaybiyyah, including the halt of al-Qaswa' and the water. Both numbers belong to that continuous report in the Book of Conditions. The citation is kept for that narration, not for every later gloss in the chapter.
